誠術百三十五月月二十三食， 其文在書籍， 學者所修， 施行日久， 官守其業，
經緯日月， 厚而未愆， 信於天文， 述而不作．
§83  The 23 eclipses in 135 months [rule] of Cheng’s method has its textual 
[basis] in the written record, refined by scholars and having been long fol-
lowed in practice. Officials have preserved it as their patrimony. It takes 
the sun and moon as warp and weft, and is solid and without blame. It is 
proved trustworthy by the patterns of heaven – [a case of being] ‘a trans-
mitter who does not innovate’ [like Confucius himself].
恂久在候部， 詳心善意， 能揆儀度， 定立術數， 推前校往， 亦與見食相應．
§84  Xun has spent a long time in the observers’ section. He had a mind for 
detail and is good at thinking, and is able to determine the graduations of 
instruments, correctly to set up the reckonings for a [given] procedure, so 
as to predict the future and compare with the past. And for its part [his 
method] corresponded to observed eclipses.
然協曆正紀， 欽若昊天， 宜率舊章， 如甲辰、 丙申詔書， 以見食為比． 今宜施用
誠術， 棄放恂術， 史官課之， 後有效驗， 乃行其法， 以審術數， 以順改易．
§85  But in harmonising the astronomical system and fixing the correct 
sequence ‘In Reverent Accord with August Heaven’ it is fitting to take 
as the formula the old patterns, such as the edicts of jiachen.41 and 
bingshen.33, while taking observed eclipses as the comparison. Now [on 
that basis] it is fitting to promulgate Cheng’s method for use. Put Xun’s 
method to one side, and let the Clerks check it; if later it should find 
verification, then one may follow its patterns, in order to have careful 
regard to the reckonings of the method, and in order to make reforms 
harmoniously.
耽以說等議奏聞， 詔書可． 恂、 整、 誠各復上書， 恂言不當施誠術， 整言不當復
恂術． 為洪議所侵， 事下永安臺覆實， 皆不如恂、 誠等言． 劾奏謾欺． 詔書報，
恂、誠各以二月奉贖罪， 整適作左校二月． 遂用洪等， 施行誠術．
§86  [The Chamberlain for Ceremonials Jiu] Chen memorialised that the report 
of Shuo and his colleagues should be given ear to, and an edict gave 
approval. Xun, Zheng and Cheng each made further submissions, Xun say-

經緯日月， 厚而未愆， 信於天文， 述而不作．
§83 The 23 eclipses in 135 months [rule] of Cheng’s method has its textual 
[basis] in the written record, refined by scholars and having been long followed in practice. Officials have preserved it as their patrimony. It takes 
the sun and moon as warp and weft, and is solid and without blame. It is 
proved trustworthy by the patterns of heaven – [a case of being] ‘a transmitter who does not innovate’ [like Confucius himself].
恂久在候部， 詳心善意， 能揆儀度， 定立術數， 推前校往， 亦與見食相應．
§84 Xun has spent a long time in the observers’ section. He had a mind for 
detail and is good at thinking, and is able to determine the graduations of 
instruments, correctly to set up the reckonings for a [given] procedure, so 
as to predict the future and compare with the past. And for its part [his 
method] corresponded to observed eclipses.
然協曆正紀， 欽若昊天， 宜率舊章， 如甲辰、 丙申詔書， 以見食為比． 今宜施用
誠術， 棄放恂術， 史官課之， 後有效驗， 乃行其法， 以審術數， 以順改易．
§85 But in harmonising the astronomical system and fixing the correct 
sequence ‘In Reverent Accord with August Heaven’ it is fitting to take 
as the formula the old patterns, such as the edicts of jiachen.41 and 
bingshen.33, while taking observed eclipses as the comparison. Now [on 
that basis] it is fitting to promulgate Cheng’s method for use. Put Xun’s 
method to one side, and let the Clerks check it; if later it should find 
verification, then one may follow its patterns, in order to have careful 
regard to the reckonings of the method, and in order to make reforms 
harmoniously.
耽以說等議奏聞， 詔書可． 恂、 整、 誠各復上書， 恂言不當施誠術， 整言不當復
恂術． 為洪議所侵， 事下永安臺覆實， 皆不如恂、 誠等言． 劾奏謾欺． 詔書報，

Cheng should each be made to redeem their offence at the cost of two

光和二年， 萬年公乘王漢上月食注． 自章和元年到今年凡九十三歲， 合百九
十六食；與官曆河平元年月錯， 以己巳為元． 事下太史令修， 上言「漢所作
注不與見食相應者二事， 以同為異者二十九事」 ．
§87  In the second year of the Guanghe period [179–180 ce], the Grandee of 
the Eighth Order Wang Han of Wan Nian submitted his observation notes 
of lunar eclipses, [running from] the first year of the Zhanghe period 
[87–88 
ce] to the current year, 93 years, with altogether 96 eclipses. It 
differed from the moons of the origin used by the official system, the 
first year of the Heping period [28 
bce], and used jisi.6 [this is the epochal 
day of the Zhuan Xu system] as its origin. The matter was referred to 
the Grand Clerk Xiu, who made a submission saying ‘In the notes com -
piled by Han there are two events which do not correspond to visible 
eclipses, and there are 29 events in which the identical have been treated 
as different.’
尚書召穀城門候劉洪． 敕曰 ： 「前郎中馮光、 司徒掾陳晃各訟曆， 故議郎蔡邕
共補續其志． 今洪其詣修， 與漢相參， 推元課分， 考校月食． 審己巳元密近， 有師
法， 洪便從漢受；不能， 對． 」
§88  The secretariat summoned Liu Hong, Watch Officer at the Gucheng 
Gate. The imperial command read: ‘Formerly the Palace Gentleman 
Feng Guang, and the Clerk of the Minister of Education Chen Huang 
each contended about the astronomical system. Thus the Gentleman for 
Consultation Cai Yong added [his report] to the relevant records. Now 
Hong is to instruct Xiu to make comparisons with Han, to push back 
to the origin and check the fractions, to examine and compare the lunar 
eclipses. If it should be found that the jisi.6 origin is accurate, and [Han] 
has a master method,
109 then let Hong accept it from Han. If not, reply 
[accordingly].’
– 3043 –
洪上言 ： 「推漢己巳元， 則考靈曜旃蒙之歲乙卯元也， 與光、晃甲寅元相經
緯． 於以追天作曆， 校三光之步， 今為疏闊． 孔子緯一事見二端者， 明曆興廢， 隨
天為節． 甲寅曆於孔子時效；己巳顓頊秦所施用， 漢興草創， 因而不易.
109 The expression ‘master method’  shi fa 師法, was in general a reference to an authoritative tradition of 
learning. Here it seems to refer to having some systematic theory rather than making predictions ad hoc.

§89  Hong’ s submission said: ‘Pushing back Han’s jisi.6 origin, then it is the 
yimao.52 origin of the Kao ling yao’s danmeng year [the 2nd out of a 
sequence of 10], which ties in with Guang and Huang’s jiayin.51 origin. 
Through the process of making an astronomical system by pursuing the 
Heavens, and comparing it with the motions of the Three Luminaries, it 
has been rejected as inaccurate. In the same way that Confucius would see 
the two ends of some single matter he considered, one must clarify the 
rise and fall of astronomical systems, while following after the standard 
set by heaven. The system using a jiayin.51 origin was correct in the time 
of Confucius, the jisi.6 Zhuan Xu origin was the one used by Qin, and 
when the Han arose they took it over as a temporary measure without 
changing it.’
至元封中， 迂闊不審， 更用太初， 應期三百改憲之節． 甲寅、 己巳讖雖有文， 略其
年數， 是以學人各傳所聞， 至於課校， 罔得厥正．
§90  When it came to the Yuanfeng period (110–105 bce) its inaccuracies became 
unacceptable, and they changed to using the Grand Inception. This was in 
accord with the rule of ‘changing the basis [of the system] every three hundred 
[years]’. As for the fact that the jiayin.51 and jisi.6 epochs have their texts 
in the Prognostications, which set out their reckonings, this is just because 
scholars have passed on the traditions they have heard. But when it comes 
to checking and comparing, they do not have the right of it.
夫甲寅元天正正月甲子朔旦冬至， 七曜之起， 始於牛初． 乙卯之元人正己巳
朔旦立春， 三光聚天廟五度． 課兩元端， 閏餘差百五十二分之三， 朔三百四， 中
節之餘二十九．
§91  In the jiayin.51 origin [year], the Celestial month-count, the first month, 
day jiazi.1, the instant of conjunction and the winter solstice coincided at 
midnight; the setting forth of the seven brightnesses [the sun, moon and 
five planets] began at the start of Ox. In the yimao.52 origin [year] [used 
by the Zhuan Xu system], the Anthropic [count] first month, day jisi.6, the 
instant of conjunction and the qi Establishment of Spring coincided at 
midnight; the three luminaries gathered together in the fifth du of House. 
Checking the starting points of the two origins, the differences in intercala -
tion excess is 3/152; the conjunctions [differ by] 304 parts, and the excess 
of central and nodal [qi] is 29.
110
110 T wo distinct Quarter Remainder systems will only differ in that their predictions of given events 
are displaced relative to one another by some fixed amount. Two of the figures given here are 
easily reproduced. Thus the Yin system has its origin in 1567 bce, a jiayin.51 year, and the con-
junction of the first civil month is predicted to fall at 58/940 day after midnight on February 23. 
The Zhuanxu system predicts that this conjunction should fall 694/940 day after midnight on

Han discussions of astronomical systems 419
以效信難聚， 漢不解說， 但言先人有書而已． 以漢成注參官施行， 術不同二
十九事， 不中見食二事． 案漢習書， 見己巳元， 謂朝不聞， 不知聖人獨有興廢
之義， 史官有附天密術． 甲寅、 己巳， 前已施行， 效後格而不用． 河平疏闊， 史
官已廢之， 而漢以去事分爭， 殆非其意． 雖有師法， 與無同． 課又不近密． 其說
蔀數， 術家所共知， 無所采取． 」遣漢歸鄉里.
§92  ‘When [it proved] difficult to assemble [evidence that his system was] veri -
fied and reliable, Han could give no explanation – all he could do was to 
say his ancestors had their books. Checking the notes collected by Han 
against the practice of the officials, there were 29 events that were not the 
same, and two that did not hit a visible eclipse. I would point out that Han 
was reading through some texts, saw the jisi.6 origin, and said to himself 
that the Court would not know about that – unaware that the Sage alone 
possesses the true righteousness for raising up and casting down, and that 
the Clerks had accurate methods for staying close to the Heavens. The 
jiayin.51 and jisi.6 [origins] had already been used before, and ceased to 
be used when they fell behind the standard. The Heping [period first year 
origin for lunar eclipses] has been rejected for inaccuracy, and the Clerks 
have already done away with it. But Han makes trouble about matters that 
are done with, which is not at all right-thinking. Even if he does have a 
“master method” it is as if he had none. Nor does the check show he is 
accurate. What he says about Obscuration reckoning is something the spe-
cialists knew already, and there is nothing to be gained from what he says.’ 
So Han was despatched back to his village.
111
February 22, which is 304/940 days earlier, as stated. In the Yin system, the 4th qi, Establishment 
of Spring of 1567 bce falls 21/32 day after midnight on February 9, whereas in the Zhuanxu system 
it falls 24/32 day after midnight on February 8, which is 29/32 days earlier, as stated. The first 
figure is more difficult to reproduce. Intercalation surplus may be calculated at any moment on 
the basis that in 235 months there are 9 complete intercalations – from which one may calculate 
the fractional (surplus) part of the accumulated intercalations at any instant after the origin. Li Rui 
shows that the figure of 3/152 is the difference of intercalation surplus between the two qi with 
which each system marks its origin, Winter Solstice preceding 1567 
bce (Yin) and Establishment 
of Spring in 1506 bce (Zhuanxu) – see Li Rui 李銳 (1768–1817) (1993), 752.
111 Not long after these events, the court at Luoyang soon ceased to function: on April 4, 190, Dong 
Zhuo 董卓 burned Luoyang and forced the emperor to shift the capital to Chang’an. Vast losses 
of documents appear to have occurred, and presumably discussions of calendrical matters were 
not a practical possibility for some time.
